conflicts: Ground-state A(99Tc): Kron et al. 2020 -107.34(8) MHz vs Wendlandt et al. 1977 -109.12(90) MHz (2 sigma). Kron et al. argue the 0.9 MHz uncertainty of the older, unresolved measurement is underestimated; the 2020 value is kept.
B(99Tc) of 4d5 5s5p 6P5/2: 57.4(38) MHz (Kron 2020) vs 93(18) MHz (Wendlandt 1977), 2 sigma; 2020 value kept.
not_found: Measured radiative lifetimes of Tc I levels: none exist as far as could be established. Palmeri, Froese Fischer, Wyart, Godefroid, MNRAS 363, 452 (2005) is a purely theoretical paper (MCHF+BP, MCDF, HFR+CP) and states that the radioactivity of all Tc isotopes is the reason for the scarcity of experimental data; its Tables 1-2 (gf values) are images on the publisher page and could not be read. No 2007 Tc I lifetime measurement was located. Theory lifetimes from Kurucz are given instead and flagged.

Measured transition probabilities / branching fractions for Tc I: none located (58 of the 70 drawn lines have no A in NIST). Only the calculated A = 4.2e7 s^-1 of the 430 nm line (Palmeri & Wyart, second-hand) is included.

Hyperfine constants of 99Tc in levels other than 6S5/2 and 4d5 5s5p 6P (e.g. 4d6 5s 6D metastables, 4d6 5p levels): Wendlandt, Bauche, Luc, J. Phys. B 10, 1989 (1977) studied the low multiplets but the paper (IOP) was not accessible.
Precise absolute transition frequencies: only wavemeter-level values (23 265.388 cm^-1 centre of gravity of 97Tc, no uncertainty) are given by Kron et al.; kept as a note, not as a frequency entry.
Measured Lande g factors beyond the NIST levels file: none located.

Wavelengths and level assignments of the second and third excitation steps of the Mainz schemes are only given graphically (Fig. 3 of Kron et al.); the exact pairing of steps was not tabulated and is described in the use string only. Raeder et al., Hyperfine Interact. 238, 15 (2017) and Mattolat et al. 2010 full texts were not accessible.
notes: Hyperfine constants and isotope shifts are from resonance ionization spectroscopy with ~100 MHz resolution (Kron et al. 2020, open access via the GSI repository). Isotope shifts are nu(first) - nu(second). All level lifetimes in this file are THEORY (Kurucz) because no measurement exists; treat them as ~25 % estimates. nuclear_moments is an extra top-level block (not in the schema) with the moments derived in the same paper.
